nodes.label: Agent workflow conventions (plan mode, subagents, verification, lessons)
nodes.norm_label: agent workflow conventions (plan mode, subagents, verification, lessons)
nodes.rationale: Repo-level operating rules: plan mode for any 3+ step or architectural task, liberal subagent delegation to keep the main context clean, a self-improvement loop writing to tasks/lessons.md after every correction, no task marked done without proof, and core principles of simplicity-first, root-cause-only fixes, and minimal blast radius.

nodes.label: @smartops/ai-agents — four Mastra agents (anomalyDetector, rootCauseAnalyzer, forecastingAgent, servicenowAgent)
nodes.norm_label: @smartops/ai-agents — four mastra agents (anomalydetector, rootcauseanalyzer, forecastingagent, servicenowagent)
nodes.rationale: Lives as an independent pnpm workspace package rather than inside the API's src/ so any future consumer (CLI, Slack bot, worker process) can import it without pulling in Fastify, and so agent tests run without an HTTP server. The package boundary also enforces discipline: the API can only call exported functions (detectAnomalies, analyzeRootCause, the Mastra instance) and cannot reach into Mastra internals. Model split is cost-driven: claude-haiku-4-5 for detection/forecasting/ServiceNow structuring, claude-sonnet-4-6 for RCA narrative. Agents are stateless, so multiple API instances can invoke them safely.

nodes.label: alertToTicket workflow (detect → RCA → approve → ticket)
nodes.rationale: Four-step Mastra workflow chaining the agents with a suspend/resume gate before ticket creation. POST /ai/workflows/alert-to-ticket starts the run, it suspends at await-approval returning { runId, status: 'suspended', rca } and writes an incident row with status pending_approval; POST /ai/workflows/:runId/resume { approved } resumes the create-ticket step and updates the row to ticketed or rejected.

nodes.label: Alertmanager (prom/alertmanager v0.27.0, :9093)
nodes.rationale: Receives notifications from VMAlert; completes the classic Prometheus-compatible alerting path alongside the AI detection path.

nodes.label: Anthropic Claude via @ai-sdk/anthropic (claude-sonnet-4-6, claude-haiku-4-5)
nodes.rationale: Integrates directly with Mastra so model swaps (Haiku <-> Sonnet) are one-line per agent. Sonnet handles the RCA narrative where reasoning quality matters; Haiku handles detection reasoning, forecasting and ServiceNow payload structuring where speed and cost dominate. The LLM only runs after a deterministic anomaly is already confirmed.

nodes.label: AWS migration path (AMP / OpenSearch / MSK)
nodes.rationale: VictoriaMetrics and Elasticsearch sit behind interfaces, so on AWS: VictoriaMetrics → Amazon Managed Prometheus, Elasticsearch → OpenSearch, Kafka → MSK, with the application logic unchanged.

nodes.label: Dead-letter topic smartops.metrics.dlq (planned)
nodes.rationale: Both Kafka consumers currently re-queue silently on ES/VM errors. A DLQ would capture failed messages for inspection and replay without blocking the main consumer group — standard production Kafka practice.

nodes.label: Drizzle ORM (PostgreSQL access + migrations)
nodes.rationale: Backs the API's PostgreSQL access with generated migrations (pnpm db:generate / db:migrate); its client pool is configured via DATABASE_URL, and PgBouncer requires ?pgbouncer=true to disable prepared statements.

nodes.label: Elasticsearch 8 (logs, metrics, traces store, :9200)
nodes.rationale: Holds OTel ECS-mapped logs (smartops-logs), Kafka-sourced metrics (smartops-metrics-*) and distributed trace spans (smartops-traces-*). The RCA agent searches it for error logs and slow/errored spans in the anomaly region + time window. Access is wrapped in withFallback() so an ES outage degrades RCA confidence instead of failing the workflow. Production: dedicated cluster with 3 master / 2 data / 2 coordinating replicas plus ILM hot-warm-cold-delete tiers; swappable for OpenSearch on AWS.

nodes.label: Elasticsearch ILM hot→warm→cold→delete tiers
nodes.rationale: Pre-configured in infra/elasticsearch/index-templates/; max_age values are the retention tuning knob.

nodes.label: Fastify 4 API (:3000) — REST routes, RBAC, SSE
nodes.norm_label: fastify 4 api (:3000) — rest routes, rbac, sse
nodes.rationale: Stateless (JWT auth, no in-process session) so it scales horizontally via replicaCount or CPU-based HPA. Hosts REST routes with Swagger, the SSE /metrics/stream endpoint, Drizzle ORM access to PostgreSQL, and imports @smartops/ai-agents in-process. Trade-off: running Mastra inside the Fastify process risks blocking the event loop on CPU-intensive workflows — a separate Mastra server process is the production upgrade path.

nodes.label: Golden signals across three regions
nodes.rationale: CPU, memory, P99 latency, error rate and requests/sec tracked for us-east-1, eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1 — the dashboard surface and the axis along which the 12 parallel detection scans are fanned out.

nodes.label: withFallback() graceful degradation
nodes.rationale: Elasticsearch and trace-fetch calls race against a 5-second timeout and catch both immediate errors (connection refused) and hangs. If ES is down the RCA agent receives empty log/trace results and writes a lower-confidence, metrics-only analysis rather than failing the workflow. Deliberate trade-off: some incidents get incomplete RCA when a data source is unavailable, but the pipeline stays running and the confidence score communicates the data-quality gap honestly.

nodes.label: Grafana 10.4 (provisioned dashboards, :3002)
nodes.rationale: Provisioned dashboards (golden signals, log explorer, asset audit) read from the same VictoriaMetrics PromQL endpoint the AI queries, so infrastructure evidence and AI evidence never diverge. Mapped to host port 3002 because 3001 is taken by the Next.js web dashboard.

nodes.label: graphify code knowledge graph (graphify-out/)
nodes.rationale: Persistent AST-derived knowledge graph with god nodes, communities and cross-file relationships; queried before grepping cold for architecture questions, rebuilt with `graphify update .` and needing no LLM/API key.

nodes.label: Helm chart infra/helm/smartops (Kubernetes deployment)
nodes.rationale: Deploys api (2 replicas, optional HPA at 70% CPU, PDB minAvailable 1), web (2 replicas), single-node VictoriaMetrics StatefulSet (50Gi, 3-month retention), Grafana, plus Bitnami PostgreSQL and Elasticsearch sub-charts. Secrets (DATABASE_URL, JWT_SECRET, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ELASTICSEARCH_PASSWORD) come from smartops-secrets rather than values. Ingress is nginx-based with /api → api and / → web.

nodes.label: Human-in-the-loop approval gate (await-approval step)
nodes.rationale: Enforced as a structural guarantee at the Mastra execution model level, not as a UI convention or an if (autoApprove) flag that could drift or be misconfigured. suspend() throws internally to halt the step — it is not a conditional return — so there is no code path that creates a ServiceNow ticket without a human calling /resume. RBAC reinforces it: only operator and admin roles can trigger RCA or approve; viewers cannot. The AI reads telemetry and produces a hypothesis but touches nothing in production.

nodes.label: Horizontal scaling strategy (stateless API + web)
nodes.rationale: Both API and web are stateless so they scale by replicaCount or HPA as-is. The one caveat is SSE: long-lived connections must reach the same API instance, so nginx ingress cookie session affinity (smartops-api, 3600s) is required. Storage sizing rule of thumb for VM: storage_GB = (metrics_per_second × 86400 × retention_days) / (10 × 1e9), i.e. ~7.8GB for 10k samples/s over 90 days.

nodes.label: simulate-infra.ts — infrastructure metric/log/trace simulator
nodes.rationale: Publishes JSON MetricMessage events to Kafka every 5s per region, pushes OTLP logs to the collector, and bulk-indexes distributed trace spans into smartops-traces-{date} every 10s. During an injected CPU anomaly the affected region's spans shift to a 35% error rate and 300ms-5s latency so the trace evidence correlates with the anomaly window and drives the RCA confidence score upward. Needs ~2 minutes of baseline before z-score detection is meaningful.

nodes.label: JWT RS256 auth + route-level RBAC (viewer/operator/admin)
nodes.rationale: Three roles enforced at the Fastify route level rather than in the UI: viewers see dashboards only; operators and admins can trigger RCA and approve tickets. Keeping enforcement server-side means the frontend never has to remember what a viewer cannot do. The SSE stream authenticates via an HttpOnly cookie so tokens never appear in URLs.

nodes.label: Kafka (apache/kafka 3.9.0, KRaft, topic smartops.metrics, :9092)
nodes.rationale: KRaft mode chosen so no ZooKeeper is required — official ASF image, single-broker local setup with 1-hour log retention. Serves as the fan-out backbone: one producer, two independent consumer groups, so adding a third sink (e.g. a Slack notifier) is a new consumer file with zero producer changes. Known gap: the MetricMessage contract is only a shared TypeScript interface, so a Schema Registry and a dead-letter topic (smartops.metrics.dlq) are the acknowledged production upgrades. Swappable for MSK on AWS.

nodes.label: Kafka fan-out pipeline (one producer, two consumer groups)
nodes.norm_label: kafka fan-out pipeline (one producer, two consumer groups)
nodes.rationale: simulate-infra.ts publishes a MetricMessage to smartops.metrics every 5s per region; consumer group smartops-vm-writer remote-writes to VictoriaMetrics and smartops-es-writer bulk-indexes to Elasticsearch (50 docs/flush). The groups are independent — stopping one does not affect the other, and neither knows the other exists — so adding a third sink is a new consumer file with zero producer change. This decoupling is the platform's stated scaling story.

nodes.label: Kafka Schema Registry (planned production upgrade)
nodes.rationale: Confluent or Redpanda with Avro/Protobuf would enforce the MetricMessage contract at runtime, catch breaking changes before consumers see them, and enable schema evolution without coordinated deploys. Explicitly listed as 'what I'd do differently — from day one'.

nodes.label: Mastra AI workflow engine (createWorkflow, suspend/resume, ^1.50.1)
nodes.rationale: Chosen because native suspend/resume — a workflow that pauses mid-execution and resumes from a different HTTP request — is the core execution primitive, not a bolt-on; that single capability determines the whole HITL architecture. Also TypeScript-native with Zod-validated inputData/resumeData, composable independent Agent instances, and direct @ai-sdk/anthropic integration. Alternatives rejected: a custom Redis queue + polling (bespoke state-persistence code and extra infra), Temporal (production-grade durable execution but requires operating a server cluster), and LangGraph/LangChain (Python-first, adds a language boundary; suspend-resume is not a first-class primitive). Accepted risks: Mastra's API surface changed significantly between 0.x and 1.x so the version is pinned, and it runs in-process with Fastify.

nodes.label: MetricMessage contract (producer ↔ consumers)
nodes.rationale: Currently a TypeScript interface shared by convention — enforced at compile time but not at runtime, so nothing catches a breaking schema change before it reaches consumers. Named as the number-one thing to do differently.

nodes.label: Next.js 14 web dashboard (:3001)
nodes.rationale: App Router + Tailwind + Recharts + SWR. Surfaces the live dashboard (SSE consumer), AI Insights, assets and alert rules, and the incident approval modal. Stateless, scales freely.

nodes.label: Un-instrumented AI layer (planned OTel spans around agent.generate())
nodes.norm_label: un-instrumented ai layer (planned otel spans around agent.generate())
nodes.rationale: The platform observes infrastructure thoroughly but the AI layer itself is a black box. Wrapping each agent.generate() call in an OTel span would surface LLM latency, tool-call counts and retries — closing what the author calls an obvious irony.

nodes.label: PgBouncer connection pooling (write-heavy path)
nodes.rationale: Recommended for high audit-log write volume; requires ?pgbouncer=true in DATABASE_URL to disable Drizzle prepared statements.

nodes.label: Playwright E2E suite (e2e/)
nodes.rationale: Covers auth, dashboard, assets and AI agent flows end to end.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL 16 (incidents, assets, alert rules, users; :5433 locally)
nodes.norm_label: postgresql 16 (incidents, assets, alert rules, users; :5433 locally)
nodes.rationale: Relational store accessed via Drizzle ORM; also backs Mastra workflow checkpoints via @mastra/pg PostgresStore so suspended runs survive API restarts and can be resumed by any API replica. Mapped to host port 5433 because 5432 is occupied by a host PostgreSQL. Scaling notes: Bitnami sub-chart read replicas, and PgBouncer connection pooling (with ?pgbouncer=true to disable prepared statements) for write-heavy audit-log workloads.

nodes.label: preDetectedAnomaly pass-through (race-condition fix)
nodes.rationale: Simulated CPU spikes last only 25 seconds, so re-running detectAnomalies() inside the workflow after the user clicks 'Trigger RCA' would often find the spike already resolved and silently return 'no anomaly found'. detectAnomalyStep therefore accepts an optional preDetectedAnomaly and returns immediately without querying VictoriaMetrics — the anomaly captured at scan time is the anomaly analyzed. The pattern generalises: any trigger source (webhook, CLI, alert rule) can inject a pre-validated anomaly event and skip re-detection.

nodes.label: RCA confidence score (0.40 base + errorLogs×0.02 + traceSpans×0.03)
nodes.norm_label: rca confidence score (0.40 base + errorlogs×0.02 + tracespans×0.03)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately honest signal of how much evidence the agent actually found rather than projected certainty: a fresh stack with no indexed logs sits at 0.40, and after 2-3 anomaly cycles it rises to 60-88%. Surfaced in the approval modal so a human reviewer can see exactly how thin the evidence is before approving. Low confidence is treated as signal, not silence — the counterpart to graceful degradation.

nodes.label: SmartOps self-monitoring (docker_stats → kubeletstats)
nodes.rationale: The OTel Collector's docker_stats receiver scrapes SmartOps's own container metrics locally; in Kubernetes it is replaced by the kubeletstats receiver (30s interval, serviceAccount auth) so the Grafana 'Asset & Audit' dashboard surfaces the platform's own resource usage.

nodes.label: ServiceNow incident creation (servicenowAgent)
nodes.rationale: Final workflow step: structures RCA output into a ServiceNow incident payload and creates the ticket over REST, returning a SNOW ticket ID that is written back onto the PostgreSQL incident row. Reachable only after a human approval resumes the workflow.

nodes.label: @smartops/shared-types (Zod schemas + TypeScript types)
nodes.rationale: Single source of contract shared across api and web; Zod also validates Mastra workflow inputData/resumeData shapes at compile time.

nodes.label: SmartOps AI Observability Platform
nodes.rationale: Full-stack AI-powered observability platform built as a pnpm + Turborepo monorepo (apps/api, apps/web, apps/ai-agents, packages/shared-types, infra, e2e). It unifies metrics, logs and traces in one dashboard and uses Mastra AI agents to detect anomalies, run RCA and auto-create ServiceNow tickets behind a human-in-the-loop gate. Framing goal: compress the on-call investigation loop from ~20 minutes of manual correlation across Grafana/Kibana/Jaeger/runbooks down to ~30 seconds.

nodes.label: Server-Sent Events metric streaming (/metrics/stream)
nodes.rationale: Chosen over WebSocket and client polling because metric streaming is strictly unidirectional server-to-client: EventSource is native with built-in exponential-backoff reconnect, works over one long-lived HTTP response through HTTP/2 multiplexing with no handshake, and Fastify's reply.raw streams it without extra plugins. Cookie auth (withCredentials + HttpOnly access cookie) keeps tokens out of URLs; named 'metrics' events avoid onmessage catching unnamed traffic. The server polls VictoriaMetrics once every 5s and broadcasts to all subscribers rather than each client polling. Trade-offs accepted: text-only (no binary framing), 6-connections-per-origin browser limit, and a need for sticky sessions (nginx cookie affinity) behind a load balancer. Binary telemetry payloads would be the trigger to revisit.

nodes.label: Turborepo (monorepo task runner with content-hash caching)
nodes.norm_label: turborepo (monorepo task runner with content-hash caching)

nodes.label: Vector log pipeline (timberio/vector 0.38, :8686)
nodes.rationale: Tails Docker container logs via the mounted docker.sock and ships them to Elasticsearch, complementing the OTLP path through the OTel Collector.

nodes.label: PostgresStore workflow state (@mastra/pg)
nodes.rationale: Mastra checkpoints live in the shared application PostgreSQL database rather than LibSQL or an in-memory store, so a suspended run survives an API restart and can be resumed by any API replica — not only the instance that started it. Removes the need for a custom job queue.

nodes.label: Deterministic z-score anomaly detection (detectAnomalies)
nodes.rationale: Pure statistical math with no LLM call: 12 parallel scans (4 metrics x 3 regions) compute a z-score against a 10-minute baseline, flagged when z > 2 AND the value clears a warning floor. Chosen over an ML model because there is no training data, no model drift, and every firing is auditable down to mean/stddev/z-score. Deterministic detection runs before probabilistic reasoning so the healthy path costs zero AI spend and sub-second latency. The threshold is deliberately conservative — lowering it to cut false negatives would push RCA work onto every minor fluctuation, compounding cost and alert fatigue. An absolute backstop (always flag CPU >= 85%) covers the cold-start case where there is not enough baseline for a meaningful z-score.
